summary: Arthur Venis was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford (B.A. ~1874–1878). He served as Professor of English (1881) and Principal (1885, 1888) at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad.

Arthur W. Ryder was an Indologist who earned his A.B. at Harvard (1894–1897), studied in Berlin, and completed a Ph.D. at Leipzig (-1901) under Karl Friedrich Geldner and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He taught Sanskrit at Harvard (1902–1906) and UC Berkeley.

Arthur Waley was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at King's College, Cambridge (1907–1910). He worked at the British Museum (1913–1929) and held an Honorary Lectureship in Chinese Poetry at SOAS University of London (1948).
Arthur Woollgar Verrall was an academic who studied at Wellington College (~1865–1869) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1873), where he later taught Robert Alexander Neil.
Aruna Haldar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose. She served as a teacher at Patna University.

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Mumbai (-1953) under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He served as a Sanskrit professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (1967–1980) and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1975–1981).

Arvind Sharma is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard. He taught at the University of Queensland (1976–1980) and held the Birks Chair in Comparative Religion at McGill University beginning in 1994.

Aryadeva was an early Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nagarjuna and Shakyamitra. He was affiliated with the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning as a colleague and taught Candrakīrti, Tilopa, and others.

Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. At the University of Kelaniya's Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, he served as Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy and Head of the Department of Buddhist Thought (attested 1993, 2006).
Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973). He served as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School (attested 1978).

Asef Bayat is a scholar of religious studies and sociology who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Kent (1978–1984). He held chairs at Leiden University (2003–2010) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2010), having previously taught at the American University in Cairo.

Asen Balikci was an ethnologist who completed his Ph.D. at Columbia University in 1956. He worked at the National Museum of Canada (~1957–1968) and served as Professor of Ethnology at the Université de Montréal from 1963 to 1993.

Ashby Butnor is a philosopher who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Hawaiʻi in 2009 under Graham Parkes and Vrinda Dalmiya. She held an appointment as Visiting Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver (attested 2011).

Ashok Aklujkar is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1965–1970). He spent his academic career in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

Ashok Gangadean is a philosopher who received his Ph.D. in philosophy from Brandeis University. He served as the Margaret Gest Professor of Global Philosophy at Haverford College, beginning in 1981, and founded the Global Dialogue Institute.

Ashok Kumar Chatterjee was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti. He headed the philosophy department at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and the Department of Philosophy and Religion at BHU (1963–1985).

Ashutosh Mukherjee was an Indian scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1880–1883). He later served at the University of Calcutta as Tagore Professor of Law (1906–1914) and in 1921–1923, and was President of The Asiatic Society (~1907–1915).

Asim Kumar Chatterjee is a scholar of Indology and archaeology who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee (~1963–1967). He was a Senior Research Fellow at Calcutta (~1967–1971) and later a lecturer in English at Jangipur College.

Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He worked at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1968) and served as a professor at the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).
Astley John Hilary Goodwin was an archaeologist who studied at Selwyn College (1919–1922) and SOAS University of London (1922). He took up an academic post at the University of Cape Town in 1923.
